On the screens where a column can be sorted (Products, Licences, Activations and Customers), click its header to sort by it. Click again to reverse the order.

The pager under the table shows "Page 2 of 7", the total number of rows, and how many rows fit on a page (10, 25, 50
or 100). If nothing matches, the table says "No ... found. Try other filters or a different search." On a screen that
has never had any rows, it explains what creates them instead.

The Customers list has a search box, columns and sorting, but no filters, so it has no filter buttons and no **Clear
filters**. The email log tabs have their own filters ([Email setup](/guide/email/#filtering-the-logs)).

## Saved views

A saved view keeps a search, the filters, the sort order and the columns of one list under a name, so you can come back
to them in one click.

1. Set up the list the way you want it.
2. Select **Save view**.
3. Type a name and confirm. A name needs at least one character and at most 60. Two views of the same list can't
   share a name.

The **Views** menu then lists your saved views for that screen. Choose one to open it. While a view is open, the menu
has **Delete this view**. A view stores its filters, search, sort and columns but not the page you were on.

Saved views belong to your user account, so other people on the site don't see them. You can keep up to 50.

## Links you can share

AccessBay keeps the state of a list in the page address, after the `#`. For example:

```text
https://example.com/wp-admin/admin.php?page=accessbay#/orders?payment=paid&q=ada&cols=customer,total
```

Filters with several values join them with commas, as in `status=active,draft`. A value that is the default is left
out, and a value AccessBay doesn't know is ignored.

Because of this:

- Reloading the page brings back the same list.
- The browser's Back and Forward buttons step through the lists you looked at.
- You can copy the address and send it to a colleague. It opens in wp-admin, so they need to be logged in with access
  to AccessBay.

The search dialog is the exception. Whatever you type there never enters the address.

## Health checks
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/health-checks/
Description: What AccessBay checks about its own server, how to read the Health screen, what each message means and how to fix it, and how to point an uptime monitor at it.

AccessBay checks the things it depends on (its secret, the database, background jobs, email, the clock, file storage
and more) and switches off only the features a failing check affects, instead of failing silently or giving wrong
answers.

## Where to see the results

- **The Health screen:** go to AccessBay > Health. This is the main place. It explains each result and offers the
  steps to fix it.
- **Site Health:** in wp-admin, go to **Tools > Site Health**. Each AccessBay check is its own test, named as in the
  table below.
- **WP-CLI:** `wp accessbay health` runs every check now and prints a table. It exits with status 1 when any check is
  critical, so it works in scripts. `--cached` prints the stored results without running anything, and
  `--format=json` prints JSON.
- **REST:** `GET /wp-json/accessbay/v1/health` returns every result and the stored alerts, for users who can manage
  AccessBay. See the [API reference](/api/).

## Reading the Health screen

The screen has one card called **Checks**, headed "What AccessBay verifies about this site, and when it last did."

### The Overall card

The first card, **Overall**, has a status label and a summary.

- When every check passes, it says "All 16 checks pass. Last ran" and the time. The number is how many checks there are.
- Otherwise it counts what needs attention, for example "2 warnings, 1 notice out of 16 checks need attention:", and lists
  each one with its status, its name and its summary. Select a name to jump to its card.

### Statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Good | The check passed. |
| Notice | Information. Nothing is wrong, or the check could not prove either way. |
| Warning | Something should be fixed, but AccessBay still works. |
| Critical | A feature that depends on this check is switched off until it is fixed. |
| Not run yet | The check has not produced a result. |

### A check's card

Every card shows the check's name, a one-line summary, its status and a message in plain words. Every result has a
message, including a good one.

When a result is a warning or critical, the card also has **What you can do**: at least one step. A step is one of two
things.

- A **link button** that opens the WordPress or AccessBay page where you fix it, such as the plugins list or the general
  settings.
- A **command or setting** in a grey box with a **Copy** button. Select **Copy** and AccessBay shows "Copied". If your
  browser refuses, it says "Could not copy. Select the text and copy it by hand." Paste WP-CLI commands into a terminal
  on your server, and paste `wp-config.php` lines into that file. Where a line needs your own value, the text is a
  placeholder such as `paste-your-long-random-secret-here`. AccessBay never puts a real secret into a step.

A notice can have no step. The card also shows the last error if there was one, when the check **Last run**, and when it
is **Next due**.

<!-- screenshot: the Health screen with the Overall card and one warning card -->

## The checks

| Check | What it looks at | At worst |
|---|---|---|
| AccessBay secret and key ids | `ACCESSBAY_SECRET` is set and valid, and every stored record can be read | Critical |
| AccessBay proxy, client IP and TLS | HTTPS, and how visitor addresses are read behind a proxy or CDN | Warning |
| AccessBay background jobs | Scheduled jobs and queued emails run on time | Critical |
| AccessBay rate limiter storage | The rate limiter can count requests | Critical |
| AccessBay database schema, engine and topology | Tables complete and InnoDB, and every query reaching the same writable server | Critical |
| AccessBay customer portal page | A published page with the portal block is chosen under Settings > General | Warning |
| AccessBay email delivery | Providers working, recent failures, credits, webhooks and the daily test email | Warning |
| AccessBay and the object cache | How AccessBay works with a persistent object cache | Notice |
| AccessBay health checks are running | The other checks have run recently | Critical |
| AccessBay server clocks | PHP's clock and time zone against the database's clock | Warning |
| AccessBay PHP requirements | The PHP version and extensions from [Requirements](/guide/requirements/) | Critical |
| AccessBay and caches in front of the site | A page cache or CDN that keeps answers it was told not to keep | Warning |
| AccessBay product entitlements | Every software product grants an entitlement | Critical |
| AccessBay release signing | Signatures verify against the published key list | Critical |
| AccessBay file storage | Release files can be written, found and removed | Critical |
| AccessBay file storage is not web-reachable | Nobody can download stored files without a licence | Critical |

A critical result switches off only what depends on it. For example, without the secret, live licences can't be
issued, and while the rate limiter can't count, the routes it protects answer `503`. Everything switches back on by
itself once the check passes again: a critical check is re-run every 10 minutes.

## What each message means

### Secret and key ids

Checks that AccessBay has a secret and that every record it stored can be opened with it. See
[The secret key](/guide/secret-key/) for how the secret works.

- **"ACCESSBAY_SECRET is malformed".** The secret AccessBay was given is not in the format it expects. Live issuance and
  live credential saves are refused. The steps offer a `define( 'ACCESSBAY_SECRET', ... )` line to correct it in
  `wp-config.php`, or restoring the key file.
- **"AccessBay is creating its test-mode key".** Reload the screen. If it stays, run `wp accessbay keys init`.
- **"The secret key file cannot be used".** The web server user can't read the file, or it is unusable. Give the web
  server user read access without making the file readable by everyone, or restore it from a backup with
  `wp accessbay keys restore`. The step `ls -l ../accessbay-private/ wp-content/accessbay-private/` shows who owns it.
- **"The secret key file is missing".** Usually the database was copied to another host, or its name or table prefix
  changed. Run `wp accessbay keys restore`, or restore the file from a backup.
- **"AccessBay is using a generated test-mode key".** Fine for testing. Before going live, run `wp accessbay keys init`,
  or define `ACCESSBAY_SECRET` in `wp-config.php`, then run `wp accessbay keys rotate`.
- **"The secret key file is waiting for its exposure check".** The file sits inside `wp-content` and AccessBay checks
  every few hours that the web can't reach it. To skip the wait, define `ACCESSBAY_SECRET` in your environment or server
  config, or move the file above the web root. `wp accessbay health` runs the check again now.
- **"AccessBay has no secret key".** On a new site run `wp accessbay keys init`. On a restored site run
  `wp accessbay keys restore`. Or define `ACCESSBAY_SECRET`.
- **"The secret equals the stored test-mode key".** Run `wp accessbay keys rotate --generate`, or set a new
  `ACCESSBAY_SECRET` and run `wp accessbay keys rotate`.
- **"The secret was exposed publicly".** Treat it as leaked. Run `wp accessbay keys rotate --generate`, then
  `wp accessbay keys rotate`.
- **"Some records are under a key no secret can open".** AccessBay answers `503` for them. Restore the key file, or list
  the old secret in `wp-config.php` with `define( 'ACCESSBAY_SECRET_PREVIOUS', 'paste-the-old-secret-here' );` and run
  `wp accessbay keys rotate`.
- **"Some records are still under an older key".** Run `wp accessbay keys rotate`.
- **"The generated test-mode key is still stored".** Run `wp accessbay keys rotate`.
- **"The secret key file needs attention".** Follow the Site Health link, then run `wp accessbay health`.
- **Good: "AccessBay has its own secret".** It names where the secret comes from and reminds you to keep a copy of the
  recovery key (`wp accessbay keys recovery`).

### Proxy, client IP and TLS

- **Good: "Proxy and TLS settings look right".**
- **Warning: "Proxy or TLS settings need attention".** It lists what it found. One finding is that the site address is
  `https` but PHP does not see the request as HTTPS, which means the server or proxy is not passing HTTPS through to
  WordPress. Others come from the request log: a CDN or proxy you did not trust, a trusted proxy that is never used, or
  forwarding headers from an untrusted source. It adds that rate limits currently count per proxy. Open WordPress Site
  Health, and run `wp accessbay proxies show` to list the proxies AccessBay trusts. The **Trusted proxies** and **Behind
  Cloudflare** settings are under Settings > Network.
- **Notice: "Proxy diagnostics are not available yet"** (or "TLS looks right; proxy diagnostics are not available
  yet"). The request-log diagnostics are not available yet. Nothing is wrong. The step shows the trusted proxies.

### Background jobs

- **Good: "AccessBay jobs are running on time".**
- **"AccessBay jobs are N minutes behind".** A warning once the delay passes the **Queue warning** setting (10 minutes by
  default), and critical at 60. Run `wp accessbay jobs run` to clear the backlog. For a lasting fix run WP-Cron from a
  system cron, with a line like
  `* * * * * cd /path/to/wordpress && wp cron event run --due-now >/dev/null 2>&1`.
- **"N background items gave up after their retries".** Open AccessBay to see them. `wp accessbay jobs list` lists them.

### Rate limiter storage

- **Good: "The rate limiter writes durably".**
- **"The rate limiter cannot write".** Limited requests answer `503`. Open Site Health, and run `wp db check`.
- **"The rate limiter does not count".** A database setting (the `CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS` flag) or a `db.php` drop-in stops it
  counting. Look at `ls -l wp-content/db.php`, then run `wp accessbay health`.
- **"Rate limiter visibility is not checked".** Add `define( 'ACCESSBAY_DB_SECOND_SESSION', true );` to
  `wp-config.php` to let AccessBay prove that a second database connection sees its writes.
- **"Rate limiter visibility is unverified".** The database refused a second connection. Ask your host about the
  per-user connection limit.
- **Critical: "Another database session does not see the rate limiter's writes".** The database is not durable or is
  split between servers, so limits could be bypassed. Unauthenticated AccessBay routes answer `503` until this passes.
  Point the site at a single database server for writes, or ask your host to, then run `wp accessbay health`.

### Database schema, engine and topology

- **Good: "The database schema and topology are sound".**
- **Critical: "The database cannot guarantee AccessBay's locks".** It lists what is wrong: a replica-routing `db.php`,
  tables that are missing or not InnoDB, missing unique keys, or a migration that did not finish. Issuing licences,
  activation, fulfilment and token redemption answer `503` until it is fixed. Validating and deactivating keep working.
  Open the plugins list to look for a database plugin, run
  `wp db query "SHOW TABLE STATUS LIKE '%accessbay%'"`, then `wp accessbay health`.

### Customer portal page

- **Good: "The customer portal page is set".**
- **Warning: "No customer portal page is set" or "The customer portal page can't be used".** The page was deleted or
  trashed, is not published, or lacks the portal block or the `[accessbay_portal]` shortcode. Choose a page under
  Settings > General > Customer portal page, or add a new page. The steps are **Open general settings** and **Add a
  new page**. See [the portal page](/guide/installation/#the-customer-portal-page).

### Email delivery

- **Good: "Email is being delivered".**
- **Warning: "Email delivery needs attention".** It lists what it found: `wp_mail` is the only provider, a provider is
  paused after repeated failures, a provider's last test failed, credits ran out or will in a number of days, a provider
  with a webhook reported nothing for 7 days, emails failed every retry in the last 24 hours, the primary provider
  failed in the last 24 hours, the site's own mail failed in the last 24 hours, or a provider refused the daily test
  email. It adds that licence keys and downloads stay on screen after purchase, so customers are not blocked. The step
  **Open email providers** takes you to the fix. See [Email setup](/guide/email/).
- **Notice: "The daily email check is on hold".** This site is not a production site, so the daily test email is held.
  Add the recipient to the staging email allowlist to try it.
- **Notice: "No email has failed recently".** The daily test email is off, so the check judges from real sends only.

### Object cache

A notice only: "A persistent object cache is in use" or "No persistent object cache is in use". AccessBay works the same
either way.

### Health checks are running

- **Good: "Health checks are running on time".**
- **Warning: "Some health checks are overdue" (with the names) or "Health checks have not run on traffic in the last 24
  hours".**
- **Critical: "Health checks have not run for over 3 days".**

Run `wp accessbay health` once, and set up a system cron as described under "When checks run" below.

### Server clocks

- **Good: "Server clocks agree".**
- **Warning: "Server clocks disagree".** The database clock and PHP's clock differ by more than 60 seconds, or PHP's
  default time zone is not UTC because a plugin or the server changed it. Times AccessBay records are still UTC. The
  steps open WordPress's general settings (time zone) and show `date -u`, the server time. Ask your host to sync the
  clocks with NTP.

### PHP requirements

- **Good: "This server has everything AccessBay needs".**
- **Critical: "This server is missing something AccessBay needs".** Typically curl with SSL or openssl. Live mode and
  outbound requests are refused until it is fixed.
- **Warning: "The PHP zip extension is missing".** Release uploads are refused. A warning "Some query filters do not apply
  to AccessBay" means something is changing the database queries.
- **Notice: "AccessBay uses WordPress's sodium_compat".** The PHP sodium extension is not loaded, so cryptography runs
  in PHP code: correct, but slower. You can ask your host to enable the extension. Nothing needs to be done otherwise.

Open Site Health's debug information, and run `php -m` to list the extensions.

### Caches in front of the site

- **Good: "No cache in front of the site ignores AccessBay's headers".**
- **Warning: "A cache in front of the site ignores AccessBay's no-store headers".** Exclude `/wp-json/accessbay/*` from
  the cache, and make uptime monitors `POST` the health ping. Open the plugins list to look for a caching plugin, then
  run `wp accessbay health`.
- **Notice: "Edge cache check unverified".** The site's name points at a private address or the test request failed, so
  AccessBay could not tell.

### Product entitlements

- **Good: "Every AccessBay software product grants an entitlement".**
- **Critical: "AccessBay software products grant no entitlement".** It is a warning if only draft products are affected.
  Licences sold for them can't be activated on a site. Products created in AccessBay get an entitlement
  automatically, so these were written another way. Archive each one and create it again under a new slug. The step
  **Open products** takes you there.

### Release signing

- **Good: "AccessBay signatures verify".**
- **Warning: "AccessBay has no published signing key list".** Run `wp accessbay keys show`, then
  `wp accessbay keys publish`.
- **Critical: "AccessBay signatures do not verify".** Compare the signing key with the published list, and publish the
  list again with `wp accessbay keys publish`. Publishing is refused until it verifies.
- **Warning: "AccessBay can't sign yet".** Neither `ACCESSBAY_SECRET` nor the secret key file is available. Run
  `wp accessbay keys init`, or define your own secret.

### File storage

- **Good: "AccessBay file storage works".**
- **Critical: "AccessBay file storage is not working".** Downloads stay off. Make sure the storage folder exists and the
  web server user may write to it. `ls -ld ../accessbay-storage accessbay-storage` shows who owns it. Then run
  `wp accessbay health`.

### File storage is not web-reachable

- **Good: "AccessBay file storage is not web-reachable".**
- **Critical: "AccessBay file storage can't be used".** The folder can't be created, or it is inside the plugins folder.
- **Critical: "AccessBay file storage is web-reachable".** A test file was served over HTTP, so paid files could be
  downloaded without a licence. Downloads stay off. Add a line like
  `define( 'ACCESSBAY_STORAGE_DIR', '/path/outside/the/web/root/accessbay-files' );` to `wp-config.php` with a folder your
  web server can write to but does not serve.
- **Warning: "File storage exposure unverified".** AccessBay could not run the test. If you know your web server does not
  serve the folder, tick "I have checked that this folder cannot be opened from the web" on the card and select
  **Confirm folder is private**. Or move the folder as above.

## When checks run

Checks run in the background on normal site traffic, on WP-Cron, and from WP-CLI. A request runs at most one check
that is due, so visitors don't notice. On a quiet site, or one that sets `DISABLE_WP_CRON`, run `wp-cron.php` or
`wp accessbay health` from a system cron every few minutes. Otherwise results grow old: the "health checks are
running" check warns, and turns critical (making the ping answer `503`) when a result is more than three days old.

The background-jobs and checks-running checks also email the site's admin address, at most once a day each, because
the queue that would normally send an alert is the thing that failed.

## Health ping for an uptime monitor

Point an external monitor at the health ping:

```sh
curl -X POST https://example.com/wp-json/accessbay/v1/health/ping
```

It answers `200` with `{"status":"ok","age":120}` while nothing is critical, and `503` with
`{"status":"critical","age":120}` when something is. `age` is the number of seconds since the newest check result
(`null` before any check has run). Use `POST`: a monitor that can only send `GET` can use the same address, but a cache
in front of the site may answer a `GET` from its copy.

The ping is limited to 60 requests a minute per client and 6000 a minute for the whole site. A `429`, or a `503` with
the error code `accessbay_temporarily_unavailable`, means the site is being flooded or its rate limiter is down, not
that a check failed. Alert on it separately from a `503` that says `"status":"critical"`.

## Settings

Two settings change how the checks behave. Both are on the Settings screen ([Plugin settings](/guide/plugin-settings/)).

- **Queue warning** (Settings > General): how many minutes a due job or queued email may wait before the
  background-jobs check warns (1 to 59, default 10). It turns critical after 60 minutes.
- **Send a daily test email** (Settings > Email settings): off by default. When on, a daily test email goes to **Daily
  test email recipient**, or to the site administrator's email when that is empty ([Email setup](/guide/email/)). An
  address alone does not turn it on.

## Installation
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/installation/
Description: Install and activate AccessBay, what activation sets up, and what deactivating or deleting it removes.

AccessBay has no public release yet. When you have the plugin's zip file, install it like any other WordPress plugin.

## Install and activate

1. Check the [requirements](/guide/requirements/).
2. In wp-admin, go to **Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin**, choose the zip file and select **Install Now**.
   Or copy the `accessbay` folder into `wp-content/plugins/` on the server.
3. Select **Activate**.

<!-- screenshot: the Plugins screen with AccessBay active and the AccessBay menu in the wp-admin sidebar -->

If the server is missing something AccessBay needs, activation stops with a page that lists each problem in plain
words, such as "AccessBay needs the PHP openssl extension". Nothing has been written to the database at that point:
fix the problem and activate again.

## What activation sets up

- AccessBay's database tables (their names start with your table prefix and `accessbay_`).
- Its capabilities. Administrators get all of them. Shop managers (a WooCommerce role) get the ones to manage
  AccessBay, manage orders and view reports, but not refunds, revealing licence keys, publishing releases or changing
  settings. If you remove a capability from a role, AccessBay does not add it back.
- The **AccessBay** menu in wp-admin, for users who can manage AccessBay.
- Every health check, due to run straight away ([Health checks](/guide/health-checks/)).

Next, set [the secret key](/guide/secret-key/).

## The customer portal page

Buyers download their files and manage their licence keys on a **customer portal page**: a normal WordPress page that
holds the AccessBay **Customer portal** block (or the `[accessbay_portal]` shortcode). The page is what the thank-you
page, the My Account menu item, the key email and the key recovery emails link to. Without it none of those links
appear, and a buyer has no way in.

- **Created for you.** The first time an administrator opens wp-admin after AccessBay is activated or updated, it adds
  a published page titled **Customer portal** with the block, and chooses it in **Settings → General → Customer portal
  page**. If a page already holds the block or the shortcode, AccessBay chooses that one instead; it never makes a
  second page. If you already chose a page, it leaves it alone.
- **Your choice wins.** AccessBay creates the page once. If you delete or trash it, or clear the setting, it does not
  make another. Choose a page again under **Settings → General**, or restore the one you deleted.
- **Health warning.** The **AccessBay customer portal page** test in **Tools → Site Health** warns when no page is
  chosen, when the page was deleted, is not published, or no longer holds the portal block or shortcode.
- **How buyers download.** The key email includes a link to the portal. There a buyer signs in, or asks for a sign-in
  link by email, and sees their licence keys and the downloads that go with them.

A key recovery or account claim email can only be sent while a portal page is chosen. If one is attempted without it,
the email is marked failed once, with an alert in the [health results](/guide/health-checks/) naming the cause, and is
not retried.

## Deactivating and deleting

Deactivating AccessBay stops its scheduled jobs and keeps everything else.

Deleting it removes only what is safe to lose: its scheduled actions and temporary data. Your tables, settings,
licences, orders, customers and user capabilities stay in the database, so a store's records don't vanish because
someone clicked **Delete**.

To remove all AccessBay data when you delete the plugin, opt in first, in either of two ways:

- Add `define( 'ACCESSBAY_REMOVE_ALL_DATA', true );` to `wp-config.php`.
- Set the option `accessbay_remove_data_on_uninstall` to true, for example with
  `wp option update accessbay_remove_data_on_uninstall 1`. On a multisite network the option is read for each site.

With the opt-in, deleting AccessBay drops its tables, deletes its `accessbay_*` options and user settings, and removes
its capabilities from every role. Other plugins' tables and options are never touched. This can't be undone, so take a
backup first.

## Introduction
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/introduction/
Description: What AccessBay is, who it is for, what it does today, and a tour of its screens.

AccessBay is a WordPress plugin for selling plugins, themes, software and other digital goods from your own site. It
is built by WPAnchorBay and released under the GPL (version 3 or later).

## What AccessBay does

- **Licensing:** licence keys, activations and seats for the software you sell.
- **Update delivery:** your customers' sites receive updates for the software they bought.
- **Protected downloads:** digital goods that only paying customers can download.

At first, orders come from WooCommerce: a paid WooCommerce order creates the matching AccessBay licence and download.
A checkout built into AccessBay, without WooCommerce, is planned for a later release. An optional AccessBay Pro plugin
will add further features on top of the free plugin. [Known limits](/guide/known-limits/) lists what the current
release leaves out.

## A tour of the screens

Open AccessBay in the WordPress admin menu. On a laptop or a wider screen, the sidebar on the left holds everything
you need to move around. There is no bar across the top.

From top to bottom, the sidebar has:

- The AccessBay logo. A "Test mode" tag sits next to it while the plugin is in test mode.
- A **Search** box. Select it, or press `/`, to search licences, customers, orders, products and settings
  ([Search and filters](/guide/finding-things/)).
- The screens, with the Dashboard first and then four groups: **Sales** (Products, Orders, Customers, Woo mapping),
  **Licensing** (Licences, Activations, API keys), **Email** (Email providers, Email settings, Email log) and
  **System** (Health, API test console, Settings). Add-ons, such as AccessBay Pro, can add items of their own, under
  **Add-ons** if they name no group.
- A footer with a link to the documentation (**Docs**) and the theme menu, where you choose a light or dark look.

On a tablet or phone, a slim bar at the top holds the logo and a menu button. The menu shows the same screens, and
also search, the theme choice, settings and docs.

Each screen starts with a title line. On a screen that sits inside another, such as one product, the title line shows
the parent first as a dimmed link, as in "Products > Add product". Select the parent to go back. The title line stays
in view when you scroll, just under the WordPress admin bar.

| Screen | What you do there |
|---|---|
| Dashboard | See store counts and the next steps to take. |
| [Products](/guide/products/) | Create and manage what you sell, its prices and its releases. |
| [Orders](/guide/orders/) | See the orders that created licences. |
| Customers | See who bought from you, with their email, company, country and join date. |
| [Licences](/guide/licences/) | Find a licence and act on it. |
| [Activations](/guide/activations/) | See which sites use a licence and deactivate one. |
| API test console | Try the licence calls against test licences. It works in test mode only. |
| Woo mapping | Link each WooCommerce product to an AccessBay product. |
| [Email log](/guide/email/#the-email-log) | See the email AccessBay and your site send. |
| [Settings](/guide/plugin-settings/) | Change how AccessBay behaves, and add email providers ([Email setup](/guide/email/)). |
| [Health](/guide/health-checks/) | See what AccessBay verified about your site, and fix what it found. |

The list screens share one layout, with a search box, filters and saved views. [Search and filters](/guide/finding-things/)
explains it once.

## Before you start

- [Requirements](/guide/requirements/): what your server needs.
- [Installation](/guide/installation/): install and activate the plugin.
- [The secret key](/guide/secret-key/): the site secret that protects stored keys and credentials.
- [Health checks](/guide/health-checks/): how AccessBay checks its own setup.
- [Email setup](/guide/email/): how AccessBay sends email.
- [REST conventions](/developers/rest-conventions/): the rules for AccessBay's REST routes.

## Known limits
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/known-limits/
Description: What this release of AccessBay leaves out, and how updating from one release to the next is meant to work.

AccessBay is a pre-release. This page lists what the current release leaves out, so you can decide whether it fits your store. The [introduction](/guide/introduction/) says what works today.

## What this release leaves out

- **Native checkout.** Orders come from WooCommerce: a paid WooCommerce order creates the matching AccessBay licence and download. A checkout built into AccessBay, which would let a store sell without WooCommerce, is planned for a later release. Until then you need WooCommerce.
- **Subscriptions.** Invoice and card renewals collected by AccessBay are planned as a Pro feature in a later release. Renewing a licence by paying again for it, through WooCommerce, is planned earlier.
- **A WordPress.org listing.** We plan to list the free plugin on WordPress.org. It is not listed yet, so you install AccessBay from a zip.

## Setting up products from the command line

You normally manage products and prices on their admin screens ([Products](/guide/products/)). WP-CLI can create them too, which is handy for scripts and for seeding a test site. A create command (`products create`, `prices add`, `customers create-guest`) prints a `Success:` line; `--format=json` prints `{"id":N}` instead and `--format=ids` prints only the new id, for scripts. The `list` and `get` commands print a table, or JSON with `--format=json`. A refused input exits with status 1 and prints the reason code, such as `duplicate_slug`. All of them work in every mode, live included.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `wp accessbay products create --type=plugin --slug=<slug> --main-file=<file> --update-uri-host=<host> [--name=<name>] [--status=draft\|active]` | Creates a product. `--type` is `plugin`, `software` or `digital`; `plugin` needs `--main-file` and `--update-uri-host`. The status defaults to `draft`. |
| `wp accessbay products list` | Lists products, up to 200. |
| `wp accessbay products get <id>` | Shows one product. |
| `wp accessbay prices add --product=<id> --amount=<minor units> --currency=<ISO code> --seats=<n> --days=<n> [--name=<name>]` | Adds a one-time price whose licence allows `<n>` seats for `<n>` days. |
| `wp accessbay prices list --product=<id>` | Lists a product's prices. |
| `wp accessbay customers create-guest --email=<address>` | Creates a guest customer. Running it again with the same address, in any letter case, returns the same customer. |

`wp accessbay licenses issue --customer=<id> --price=<id>` then issues a licence for what you created.

## Updating from one release to the next

Moving from one release to the next is meant to keep every licence, activation and release you have. Refusing a downgrade, with a message that names both versions and says how to roll back, is planned too. Neither has been tested yet.

Until they are:

- Back up your database before you update.
- Keep the zip of the release you are replacing, so that you can go back to it.

## Licence
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/licence/
Description: The licences AccessBay and its client SDK are released under, what they mean for plugins you build with the SDK, and how to get the source.

AccessBay's plugins are released under the GNU General Public Licence, version 3 or later (GPL-3.0-or-later). The client SDK that you include in the plugins and themes you sell is released under version 2 or later (GPL-2.0-or-later). This page says what each licence covers and what we have not settled. It is not legal advice.

## The AccessBay plugins

The free AccessBay plugin, the AccessBay Pro plugin, and the code compiled into them are GPL-3.0-or-later. Each plugin's header and `readme.txt` say so.

We chose version 3 because the free plugin bundles Action Scheduler, which is GPL-3.0-or-later and can't be distributed under version 2.

What this means for you as a vendor:

- You may use, modify and redistribute the plugins under the GPL. Anyone who receives a copy may do the same.
- The GPL grants no trademark rights. A redistributed or modified copy can't call itself AccessBay.
- Pro is GPL as well. What you pay for is updates, support, licence-key activation and hosted features, not the right to use the code.

## The client SDK in your own plugins

The SDK is released under GPL-2.0-or-later. We chose the widest GPL variant on purpose: the SDK is embedded in other people's plugins, and a plugin released under any GPL licence can include it. The SDK doesn't bundle Action Scheduler or any Apache-2.0 code, which is why it doesn't need version 3.

The SDK package is meant to be prefixed with Strauss when you include it in your plugin. The [SDK page](/developers/sdk/) will carry the full steps when the SDK is released.

A plugin that includes the SDK is subject to the GPL. When you distribute it, you distribute a combined work, and the whole of it has to go out under terms that are compatible with the GPL. This page is not legal advice. Ask a lawyer how it applies to your own plugin.

## Where the source is

- **PHP:** the plugin's own PHP files ship in the zip as they are in the repository. Strauss gives the classes of most bundled libraries a prefix. Action Scheduler is the exception: the free plugin bundles it unprefixed. A few development files, such as tests, build configuration, `composer.lock` and the UI demo page, are left out.
- **Admin screens:** the zip carries the compiled JavaScript for the admin screens, without its human-readable source. Putting that source in the zip, through source maps or a link, is planned and has not been done yet.
- **How to get the source today:** each zip is offered for download with a source archive for the same version, as a separate download beside it. If you can't find the archive for the version you hold, write to {source request address} with that version and we send it to you.
- **The repository:** it is private, so it is not a public source link.

## Licences
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/licences/
Description: The Licences screen, what each column and status means, and how to filter licences.

Go to AccessBay > Licences to see the licences you have issued. AccessBay issues them automatically when an order is
paid. Until the first one exists the screen says so. Search, filters, saved views and shareable links are described in
[Search and filters](/guide/finding-things/).

## Columns

| Column | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Key | The licence key, masked so only its last four characters show. Select it to open the licence. An "Imported" tag marks a key that was imported rather than generated by AccessBay. |
| Status | The licence's status. See below. |
| Sites | How many sites use the licence out of how many it allows, for example "3 of 5", or "3 of unlimited". |
| Expires | The day the licence ends, or "No expiry". |
| Created | The day the licence was created. |

Click **Expires** or **Created** to sort by it.

## Statuses

- **Not started:** the licence's access has not begun yet.
- **Active:** the licence gives access now.
- **Expired:** its access has ended.
- **Suspended:** it is on hold, either because someone put it on hold or because of a dispute.
- **Revoked:** someone withdrew it.
- **Void:** no purchase counts toward it any more, for example because all of them were reversed.

## Filters and search

- **Status:** Not started, Active, Expired, Suspended, Revoked, Void.
- **Key origin:** Generated, Imported.

The search box finds a licence by its id, by the last four characters of its key, or by the whole key pasted in. A
pasted key is looked up and never saved or shown back.

## Orders
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/orders/
Description: The Orders screen, what each column and status means, and how to filter orders.

Go to AccessBay > Orders to see the orders AccessBay knows about. The list is read-only and shows the newest order
first. Orders from WooCommerce and from checkout appear here as they are placed. Search, filters, saved views and
shareable links are described in [Search and filters](/guide/finding-things/).

## Columns

| Column | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Order | The order number. Select it to open the order. |
| Customer | The buyer's email address. |
| Source | Where the order came from: WooCommerce, AccessBay checkout, Manual or API. |
| Payment | Where the money stands. A "Disputed" tag appears next to it when the buyer has opened a dispute. |
| Fulfilment | Whether the buyer has received what they bought, such as a licence. |
| Total | The order total in its currency. |
| Placed | The day the order was placed. |

You can hide any column with the columns button. This list has no sort by column.

## Payment

- **Pending:** the payment has not come in yet.
- **Paid:** the payment came in.
- **Partly refunded** and **Refunded:** part of the money, or all of it, went back to the buyer.
- **Charged back:** the buyer's bank took the money back.
- **Cancelled:** the order was cancelled.

## Fulfilment

- **Not fulfilled:** nothing has been delivered yet.
- **Partly fulfilled** and **Fulfilled:** some or all of the order has been delivered.
- **Partly revoked** and **Revoked:** some or all of what was delivered has been taken back.
- **Nothing to fulfil:** the order has nothing to deliver.

## Filters and search

- **Source:** WooCommerce, AccessBay checkout, Manual, API.
- **Payment:** Pending, Paid, Partly refunded, Refunded, Charged back, Cancelled.
- **Fulfilment:** Not fulfilled, Partly fulfilled, Fulfilled, Partly revoked, Revoked, Nothing to fulfil.

Each filter takes several values, and different filters combine. For example, "Payment: Paid, Partly refunded" together
with "Fulfilment: Not fulfilled" lists paid orders that haven't been delivered.

The search box finds an order by its number or by the buyer's email address.

## Plugin settings
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/plugin-settings/
Description: How the Settings screen works, what every setting does, how to show AccessBay in the admin bar, and how to erase all AccessBay data.

## The Settings screen

Go to AccessBay > Settings. The screen has sections: **General**, **Email settings**, **Network**, **Logging**,
**Licensing** and **Plugin**. API keys and Email providers have their own entries in the sidebar. To jump straight to a
setting, [search for it](/guide/finding-things/#settings-in-the-results).

- A setting that is on or off is a full-width row: its name and help text on the left and a switch on the right.
  Select anywhere on the row to flip it.
- Nothing changes until you select **Save changes**. AccessBay then shows "Settings saved".
- If you leave the screen with unsaved changes, AccessBay asks "Leave without saving?".

## All settings

| Section | Setting | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| General | Mode | Test marks new orders and licences as test ones, so they stay apart from real ones. Live is for real customers. |
| General | New order origin | Where new orders start: WooCommerce, AccessBay's own checkout, or both while you switch over. |
| General | Archived products | Keep updates: customers with a valid licence keep downloads and updates after you archive a product, until their licence expires. Stop updates: archiving ends downloads and updates for everyone. Archiving always ends new sales. |
| General | Event retention | How many days events are kept before they are deleted (1 to 3650). |
| General | Queue warning | Minutes a queued job may wait before the background-jobs check warns (1 to 59). See [Health checks](/guide/health-checks/). |
| General | Customer portal page | The ID of the page that shows the customer portal. 0 means none. |
| General | Support email | The address customers see on the thank-you page and in the portal when they need help. Empty shows none. |
| Email settings | Email record retention | Days to keep AccessBay emails, their attempts, provider events and the site mail log. 0 keeps everything (0 to 3650). |
| Email settings | Email retry period | Days a failed email keeps being retried before it is given up (1 to 5). |
| Email settings | Staging email allowlist | On a staging site, email goes only to these addresses and to site administrators. |
| Email settings | Send a daily test email | Once a day, send a short test email through each mail provider. Off by default. |
| Email settings | Daily test email recipient | Where the daily test email goes. Empty uses the site administrator address. |
| Email settings | Mail problem alerts | Who is emailed when a mail provider stops working and again when it works, up to ten addresses. Empty uses the site administrator address. |
| Network | Trusted proxies | Your own proxies, one IP address or CIDR range per line. Their forwarded client address is trusted. |
| Network | Behind Cloudflare | Trust Cloudflare's forwarded client address. |
| Logging | Request log retention | Days to keep request log rows (1 to 90). |
| Logging | Request log size | The most rows the request log keeps, the oldest going first (1000 to 1,000,000). |
| Licensing | Access deadline cap | The longest an access deadline may be set ahead, in days (1 to 365). |
| Licensing | Licence key prefix | The letters every new licence key starts with. |
| Licensing | Staging activations | The most staging sites a licence may keep active at once. 0 turns the allowance off (0 to 1000). |
| Plugin | Delete data when the plugin is deleted | See below. |
| Plugin | AccessBay in the admin bar | See below. |

The [email setup](/guide/email/) page explains the email settings in context, and
[Health checks](/guide/health-checks/) explains Queue warning.

## The Plugin section

The Plugin section holds the settings about the plugin itself rather than your store. Both settings are off until you
turn them on.

## AccessBay in the admin bar

Turn this on to add an AccessBay link, with the AccessBay icon, to the bar at the top of the WordPress admin. It opens
the AccessBay home.

- After you select **Save changes**, the link appears or disappears at once. You don't need to reload the page.
- It shows only in the admin, never on your site's pages.
- It shows only to people who may open AccessBay.
- The icon takes its colours from the admin colour scheme the person chose in their WordPress profile, including the
  hover colour, and it follows a browser's forced-colours mode.

## Delete data when the plugin is deleted

When you delete AccessBay from the Plugins screen, it always stops its background jobs and removes its temporary data.
Your products, licences, orders and customers stay, so you can install AccessBay again and carry on.

Turn this setting on if you want deleting the plugin to remove everything instead: AccessBay's database tables, its
settings, its products, its licence and API keys, its secret key file and its stored files. This cannot be undone, so
make a backup first. Only site administrators see this setting. On a multisite network only super admins see it, and
it applies to one site at a time. The folder of stored files stays while another site on the network uses the same
folder.

You can also opt in for every site at once by setting `ACCESSBAY_REMOVE_ALL_DATA` to `true` in your site's
configuration file.

## Erase all data

Erase all data removes the same things as deleting the plugin with the setting above turned on, but keeps AccessBay
installed and active. AccessBay then sets itself up again, as on a fresh install: it creates its tables again, gives
the default roles their capabilities back and runs its health checks again. Use it to start over, for example after
testing on a staging site.

- Only a site administrator can do it. On a multisite network only a super admin can.
- You type `ERASE` to confirm and enter your own WordPress password. A wrong password erases nothing, and the audit log
  records the attempt (never the password). After five tries in 15 minutes you wait before you can try again.
- If AccessBay made a secret key file for your site, it makes a new one. Download its new recovery key afterwards
  ([The secret key](/guide/secret-key/)). A secret you set in your site's configuration file stays as it is.
- AccessBay goes back to test mode and its default settings.
- If AccessBay Pro is active, its data (saved payment methods) is erased too.
- On a multisite network only the current site is erased. The folder of stored files stays when another site on the
  network uses the same folder, and the audit log says so.
- The erase is recorded in AccessBay's audit log, with who did it and when.

If something stops the erase partway, AccessBay says so and records it in the audit log when it can. Run it again to finish; running it twice does no harm.

## Products
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/products/
Description: The Products screen, its columns and filters, and what the Draft, Active and Archived statuses mean.

Go to AccessBay > Products to see everything you sell: plugins, downloads and bundles. The screen works like the other
lists, so search, filters, saved views and shareable links are described in
[Search and filters](/guide/finding-things/). Select **Add product** to create one.

Until you add the first product the screen says "No products yet". Add the first plugin, download or bundle you sell.

## Columns

| Column | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Product | The product's name. Select it to open the product. |
| Type | Software, Digital download or Bundle. |
| Status | Draft, Active or Archived. |
| Prices | How many prices the product has. |

Click **Product** to sort by name. You can hide the Type, Status and Prices columns with the columns button.

## Filters and search

- **Status:** Draft, Active, Archived. Tick more than one to see several at once.
- **Type:** Software, Digital download, Bundle.

The search box matches part of a product's name or slug.

## Statuses

- **Draft.** Customers can't buy it. A new product starts here.
- **Active.** Customers can buy it. An active product with no active price can't be bought yet, and the product screen
  says to add a price on its **Pricing** tab.
- **Archived.** Customers can no longer buy it. Its prices, orders and licences stay, and it can't be activated again.
  Whether existing customers keep their downloads and updates depends on the **Archived products** setting under
  Settings, General.

The product screen has three tabs: **Details**, **Pricing** and **Releases**. The title line shows "Products" as a dimmed
link before the product's name, which takes you back to the list.

## Brevo
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/providers/brevo/
Description: How to connect Brevo (formerly Sendinblue) to AccessBay - authenticate a domain, create an API key, fill in the form and set up delivery events.

Brevo was called Sendinblue before.

## Before you start

In Brevo, authenticate your sending domain. Brevo asks for these DNS records:

- a TXT record with the Brevo code,
- DKIM, as one TXT record or two CNAME records,
- a DMARC TXT record.

SPF and MX records are not required for this. The free plan allows up to 300 emails a day once Brevo has approved your
account. See [Brevo's pricing](https://www.brevo.com/pricing/).

## Get the key

1. In Brevo, go to Settings > SMTP & API > **API keys**.
2. Select **Generate a new API key**, name it, and copy it. Brevo shows it once.

Brevo may also limit which IP addresses can use a key. If the test fails with an "unrecognised IP" message, look at
Brevo's security settings and allow your server's address.

## Fill in AccessBay

Go to Settings > Email providers, select **Add provider** and pick **Brevo**.

| AccessBay field | Where the value comes from |
|---|---|
| Name | Any name you like. |
| From address | An address on the authenticated domain, or a verified sender. |
| API key | The key from "Get the key". |
| Webhook bearer token | A token you make up, and also enter as the webhook's bearer authentication in Brevo. Leave empty if you skip webhooks. |

**Test connection** checks the key against your Brevo account. It sends no email.

## Delivery events (webhook)

Brevo sends events such as delivered, soft bounce, hard bounce, spam, blocked, invalid, deferred and error.

1. In AccessBay, copy the **Webhook URL** from the **Webhooks** card.
2. Choose a long random token. Enter it in **Webhook bearer token** in AccessBay and save.
3. In Brevo, add a transactional webhook with that URL. In Brevo's menu this may be under Transactional > Settings >
   Webhook, but check Brevo's documentation for the current location.
4. Set the webhook's authentication to bearer, with the same token. Brevo's documentation describes bearer
   authentication for its API (`POST /v3/webhooks`). If the dashboard has no field for it, create the webhook through
   the API.
5. Tick the events you want.

## Common errors

- **"Unrecognised IP" in the test.** The key is limited to certain IP addresses. Allow your server's address in Brevo.
- **Brevo refuses the email.** The sender or domain isn't verified, or the account isn't approved yet.
- **No delivery events arrive.** The bearer token in Brevo must be exactly the one in AccessBay.

## Vendor documentation

- [Authenticate your domain](https://help.brevo.com/hc/en-us/articles/12163873383186-Authenticate-your-domain-with-Brevo-Brevo-code-DKIM-DMARC)
- [API key authentication](https://developers.brevo.com/docs/api-key-authentication)
- [Transactional webhooks](https://developers.brevo.com/docs/transactional-webhooks)
- [Webhook authentication](https://developers.brevo.com/docs/username-and-password-authentication)

## Mailgun
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/providers/mailgun/
Description: How to connect Mailgun to AccessBay - add and verify a domain, get an API key, fill in the form and set up delivery events.

Mailgun is a Sinch company. AccessBay shows this provider as **Mailgun (API)**.

## Before you start

1. In Mailgun, add your sending domain. A subdomain such as `mg.example.com` keeps your main domain's mail separate.
2. Add the DNS records Mailgun shows for the domain: an SPF record (`v=spf1 include:mailgun.org ~all`), a DKIM TXT
   record, a tracking CNAME pointing to `mailgun.org`, and MX records (`mxa.mailgun.org` and `mxb.mailgun.org`, priority
   10).
3. Wait until Mailgun marks the domain as verified. This can take up to 48 hours. An unverified domain has a limit of
   300 emails a day.

Mailgun keeps the US and EU regions apart. An account and its domain exist in one region only.

## Get the key

Mailgun has two kinds of key:

- **Domain sending key.** Created under Sending > Domains > your domain > Domain Settings > Sending API keys > **Add
  Sending Key**. It can only send, and Mailgun shows it once.
- **Account API key.** Found under Account Settings > API Keys.

A domain sending key is the narrowest choice. But **Test connection** in AccessBay reads the domain's record from
Mailgun, and a sending-only key may be refused for that call. If the test fails with an authentication error although
the key and region are right, use the account API key instead.

## Fill in AccessBay

Go to Settings > Email providers, select **Add provider** and pick **Mailgun (API)**.

| AccessBay field | Where the value comes from |
|---|---|
| Name | Any name you like. |
| From address | An address on the verified domain. |
| API key | The key from "Get the key". |
| Sending domain | The domain you verified in Mailgun, for example `mg.example.com`. |
| Region | **US** (`api.mailgun.net`) or **EU** (`api.eu.mailgun.net`). It must match the region of your Mailgun account. |
| Webhook signing key | Mailgun > Settings > API Security > HTTP webhook signing key. Leave empty if you skip webhooks. |

The signing key is the same for the whole account and is separate from your API keys.

**Test connection** checks the key and the sending domain. It sends no email.

## Delivery events (webhook)

1. In AccessBay, copy the **Webhook URL** from the **Webhooks** card.
2. In Mailgun, add an HTTP webhook for each of these events: delivered, permanent failure, temporary failure,
   complained and unsubscribed. Mailgun's documentation says webhooks are under Sending > Webhooks, and that you can set
   them for a domain or for the whole account. The menu may look different in your account.
3. Paste the URL for each event. Mailgun allows up to three URLs per event type, and needs HTTPS with a certificate
   from a public certificate authority.
4. Copy the HTTP webhook signing key into **Webhook signing key** in AccessBay and save.

## Common errors

- **Authentication errors.** The region is wrong, or the key is a sending key that the test can't use. Check the
  **Region** first.
- **The domain is not found.** The **Sending domain** must match the domain in Mailgun exactly.
- **Mailgun refuses the email.** The domain is not verified yet. Check the DNS records.

## Vendor documentation

- [Verify a domain](https://documentation.mailgun.com/docs/mailgun/user-manual/domains/domains-verify)
- [API authentication and key types](https://documentation.mailgun.com/docs/mailgun/api-reference/authentication)
- [Configuring webhooks](https://documentation.mailgun.com/docs/mailgun/user-manual/webhooks/configuring-webhooks)
- [Securing webhooks](https://documentation.mailgun.com/docs/mailgun/user-manual/webhooks/securing-webhooks)

## Email providers
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/providers/overview/
Description: Which email provider to choose for AccessBay, where the webhook URL is shown, how to test, and a setup page for each provider.

AccessBay can send through several email providers at once. This page helps you pick one. Each provider has its own
page with the steps to get its key, the values to enter in AccessBay, and what to do when something fails. For the
rest of the email system (failover, retries, alerts, the email log), see [Email setup](/guide/email/).

## Which provider to choose

| You want to | Choose |
|---|---|
| Keep using a mail plugin such as WP Mail SMTP, FluentSMTP or Post SMTP | [WordPress (wp_mail)](/guide/providers/wp-mail/) |
| Send through a mailbox you already have (your host, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365) | [SMTP](/guide/providers/smtp/) |
| Send through a transactional email service and see delivered and bounced emails in AccessBay | [Twilio SendGrid](/guide/providers/sendgrid/), [Mailgun](/guide/providers/mailgun/), [Postmark](/guide/providers/postmark/), [Resend](/guide/providers/resend/), [Brevo](/guide/providers/brevo/) or [SMTP2GO](/guide/providers/smtp2go/) |
| Use Zoho's service | [ZeptoMail](/guide/providers/zeptomail/) (no delivery events in this version) |

If you have no preference, pick a service from the third row. Those providers can tell AccessBay when an email was
delivered, bounced or marked as spam. `wp_mail`, SMTP and ZeptoMail can only report that the email was accepted.

Choose **WordPress (wp_mail)** when a plugin such as WP Mail SMTP or FluentSMTP should do the sending. AccessBay hands
the email to WordPress, and the plugin sends it with the settings you gave the plugin. You don't enter any key in
AccessBay for this.

It is a good idea to add at least two providers. If one fails, AccessBay tries the next.

## Steps that every provider needs

1. Create an account with the provider.
2. Verify the sender address or the sending domain in the provider's account. Most providers refuse an email from an
   address they have not verified. Each provider page says how.
3. Create a key (or token, or password) for sending.
4. In AccessBay, go to Settings > Email providers, select **Add provider**, pick the provider and fill in the form.
   The provider page lists each field.
5. Select **Save and test**.
6. Optional: set up the webhook so the provider reports delivery. See below.

## Where the webhook URL is shown

A webhook lets the provider tell AccessBay that an email was delivered, bounced or reported as spam.

Each provider that supports webhooks has its own URL. In AccessBay, go to Settings > Email providers and find the
**Webhooks** card. It lists a **Webhook URL** for the provider, with a copy button. Paste that URL into the provider's
webhook settings. Then enter the secret the provider gives you (or the user name and password you chose) in the
provider's form in AccessBay.

The URL belongs to one provider. If you add two providers of the same type, each has its own URL.

AccessBay refuses a webhook call that fails the check. If the provider's dashboard shows an HTTP 401 answer from
your site, the secret in AccessBay does not match the one in the provider.

`wp_mail`, SMTP and ZeptoMail have no webhook.

## Test a provider

Two buttons in the **Actions** column of the Email providers table help you check a setup:

- **Test connection** checks the key or login. For most providers it sends no email. SMTP2GO and ZeptoMail can't
  check a key without sending, so for them it sends one test email to your own admin address.
- **Send test email** sends one short email to an address you type, through that provider only. If it fails, no other
  provider takes over.

If **Save and test** fails, the dialog stays open and shows the reason. Fix the field and try again. Keys, tokens and
passwords are stored encrypted and are never shown again. To change one, select **Edit** and enter the new value.

## The provider pages

- [Twilio SendGrid](/guide/providers/sendgrid/)
- [Mailgun](/guide/providers/mailgun/)
- [Postmark](/guide/providers/postmark/)
- [Resend](/guide/providers/resend/)
- [Brevo](/guide/providers/brevo/)
- [SMTP2GO](/guide/providers/smtp2go/)
- [ZeptoMail](/guide/providers/zeptomail/)
- [SMTP](/guide/providers/smtp/) (Google Workspace and Gmail, Microsoft 365, your host)
- [WordPress (wp_mail)](/guide/providers/wp-mail/)

Vendors change their dashboards. If a menu name here does not match what you see, use the vendor's documentation
linked on each page.

## Postmark
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/providers/postmark/
Description: How to connect Postmark to AccessBay - confirm a sender, copy the server API token, fill in the form and set up delivery events.

## Before you start

Postmark refuses an email from an address it hasn't verified. It answers with an HTTP 422 error. Do one of these in
Postmark:

- Confirm a **Sender Signature** for the From address.
- Verify the whole domain. This needs DKIM records. Postmark also recommends a custom Return-Path, which is a CNAME
  record pointing to `pm.mtasv.net`.

A new Postmark account starts with limits, such as 100 test emails a month on the free plan. Check Postmark's pages for
what applies to your account.

## Get the key

1. In Postmark, open your **Server** (Servers > your server).
2. Open the **API Tokens** tab.
3. Copy the **Server API token**.

Don't use the Account API token. It can only manage servers, not send mail.

## Fill in AccessBay

Go to Settings > Email providers, select **Add provider** and pick **Postmark**.

| AccessBay field | Where the value comes from |
|---|---|
| Name | Any name you like. |
| From address | A confirmed Sender Signature or an address on the verified domain. |
| Server API token | The token from "Get the key". |
| Message stream | Leave empty for the default transactional stream (`outbound`). Enter a stream's name only if you use another one. |
| Webhook username | A user name you choose. Leave empty if you skip webhooks. |
| Webhook password | A password you choose. |

**Test connection** checks the token. It sends no email.

## Delivery events (webhook)

Postmark doesn't sign webhooks. It uses basic authentication, with the user name and password inside the URL.

1. In AccessBay, copy the **Webhook URL** from the **Webhooks** card.
2. Choose a user name and a password. Enter them in **Webhook username** and **Webhook password** in AccessBay and
   save.
3. In Postmark, open your server's webhook settings and add a webhook. Use the AccessBay URL with the pair in front
   of the host: `https://user:password@your-site.example/...`.
4. Tick **Delivery**, **Bounce** and **Spam complaint**.
5. Postmark's **Verify webhook** button sends a test for each event. Use it to check the setup.

Postmark's menu names and per-stream webhook options may differ from this description. See Postmark's webhook guide
below.

## Common errors

- **HTTP 422 from Postmark.** The From address is not a confirmed sender or on a verified domain.
- **The test fails with an authentication error.** You may have copied the Account API token. Use the Server API token.
- **No delivery events arrive.** Check that the user name and password in the URL match the two fields in AccessBay.

## Vendor documentation

- [Account and server API tokens](https://postmarkapp.com/support/article/1008-what-are-the-account-and-server-api-tokens)
- [Getting started](https://postmarkapp.com/support/article/1002-getting-started-with-postmark)
- [Sender Signatures](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/user-guide/managing-your-account/managing-sender-signatures)
- [Webhooks overview](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/webhooks/webhooks-overview)

## Resend
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/providers/resend/
Description: How to connect Resend to AccessBay - verify a domain, create a sending-only API key, fill in the form and set up delivery events.

## Before you start

In Resend, add and verify your sending domain. Resend shows the DNS records to add at your DNS host. Resend refuses an
email whose From address is on a domain that isn't verified.

The free plan allows 100 emails a day, 3,000 a month and 3 domains. Check [Resend's pricing](https://resend.com/pricing)
for current limits.

## Get the key

1. In Resend, go to **API Keys** and select **Create API Key**.
2. Name it, for example "AccessBay".
3. Set the permission to **Sending access**. If you like, limit it to your one domain.
4. Copy the key. Resend shows it once.

AccessBay accepts a key that can only send.

## Fill in AccessBay

Go to Settings > Email providers, select **Add provider** and pick **Resend**.

| AccessBay field | Where the value comes from |
|---|---|
| Name | Any name you like. |
| From address | An address on the verified domain. |
| API key | The key from "Get the key". |
| Webhook signing secret | The secret that starts with `whsec_`, shown on the webhook's page in Resend. Leave empty if you skip webhooks. |

**Test connection** checks the key. It sends no email.

## Delivery events (webhook)

1. In AccessBay, copy the **Webhook URL** from the **Webhooks** card.
2. In Resend, go to **Webhooks** and select **Add Webhook**. Paste the URL.
3. Tick the events: `email.delivered`, `email.bounced`, `email.complained`, `email.delivery_delayed`, `email.failed`
   and `email.suppressed`.
4. Save, open the webhook and copy its signing secret (it starts with `whsec_`).
5. Paste it into **Webhook signing secret** in AccessBay and save.

## Common errors

- **The test fails with an authentication error.** The key is wrong or was deleted. Create a new one.
- **Resend refuses the email.** The From address is on a domain that isn't verified yet. While a domain is not
  verified, Resend may allow test emails only to your own address. AccessBay treats this refusal as a setup problem
  with the provider, not as a problem with the email, so verify the domain and test again.
- **No delivery events arrive.** Check that the secret in AccessBay is the one from the same webhook.

## Vendor documentation

- [Domains](https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/domains/introduction)
- [Create an API key](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/api-keys/create-api-key)
- [Event types](https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/webhooks/event-types)
- [Verify webhook requests](https://resend.com/docs/dashboard/webhooks/verify-webhooks-requests)

## Twilio SendGrid
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/providers/sendgrid/
Description: How to connect Twilio SendGrid to AccessBay - verify a sender, create an API key, fill in the form and set up delivery events.

AccessBay shows this provider as **Twilio SendGrid (API)**. It sends through SendGrid's web API.

## Before you start

You need a SendGrid account and a verified sender. Use one of these:

- **Domain authentication** (best for production). In SendGrid, go to Settings > Sender Authentication > Domain
  Authentication and select **Get Started**. SendGrid shows DNS records to add at your DNS host: by default three CNAME
  records and one DMARC TXT record. With automated security turned off, it shows one MX and three TXT records
  instead. Add them, then verify in SendGrid.
- **Single sender**. Go to Marketing > Senders, add the address, then select the link SendGrid emails to that address.

The **From address** in AccessBay must belong to the verified domain or be the verified single sender.

## Get the key

1. In SendGrid, go to Settings > API Keys and select **Create API Key**.
2. Name it, for example "AccessBay".
3. Choose **Custom Access**, then set **Mail Send** to **Full Access**. Nothing else is needed.
4. Select **Create & View** and copy the key. SendGrid shows it once.

A key without the Mail Send permission fails the test.

## Fill in AccessBay

Go to Settings > Email providers, select **Add provider** and pick **Twilio SendGrid (API)**.

| AccessBay field | Where the value comes from |
|---|---|
| Name | Any name you like. |
| From address | A verified sender or an address on the authenticated domain. |
| From name | Optional. |
| API key | The key from step 4 above. |
| Region | **Global** (`api.sendgrid.com`) for most accounts. **EU** (`api.eu.sendgrid.com`) only if you use an EU subuser. EU sending needs the Pro plan or above. The field is required. |
| Webhook verification key | The public key from the signed event webhook (see below). Leave empty if you skip webhooks. |

**Test connection** checks that the key can send mail. It sends no email.

## Delivery events (webhook)

1. In AccessBay, copy the **Webhook URL** from the **Webhooks** card.
2. In SendGrid, go to Settings > Mail Settings > Webhook Settings > Event Webhooks and create a webhook with that URL.
3. Tick the events: delivered, bounce, dropped, spam report and unsubscribe. AccessBay counts a dropped event as a hard
   bounce.
4. Turn on **Enable Signed Event Webhook** and save.
5. The key pair exists only after you save. Reopen the webhook (cog icon, then **Edit**) and copy the public
   verification key.
6. Paste it into **Webhook verification key** in AccessBay and save.

Don't use SendGrid's test button before step 5 is done. Until the key is in AccessBay, the signature can't be checked.

## Common errors

- **The test fails with a permission message.** The key lacks Mail Send. Create a new key as in "Get the key".
- **The test fails on an EU account.** Check the **Region**. The EU host needs an EU subuser, and the Pro plan or above.
- **SendGrid refuses the email.** The From address is not verified. Verify the sender or domain.
- **No delivery events arrive.** Check that the signed event webhook is on, and that the verification key in AccessBay
  is the public key of the same webhook.

## Vendor documentation

- [API keys](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/ui/account-and-settings/api-keys)
- [Domain authentication](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/ui/account-and-settings/how-to-set-up-domain-authentication)
- [Single sender verification](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/ui/sending-email/senders)
- [Signed event webhook](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/for-developers/tracking-events/getting-started-event-webhook-security-features)

## SMTP
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/providers/smtp/
Description: How to connect any SMTP server to AccessBay - Google Workspace and Gmail, Microsoft 365, or your host's mailbox.

Use the SMTP provider for any mail server that takes mail over SMTP. For SMTP2GO, Brevo and the other services in this
guide, their own provider type is better, because it can report delivery.

## Before you start

You need a mailbox on the server, with its address and password. The **From address** should be that mailbox's
address, or one the server allows you to send as.

## Fill in AccessBay

Go to Settings > Email providers, select **Add provider** and pick **SMTP**.

| AccessBay field | Where the value comes from |
|---|---|
| Name | Any name you like. |
| From address | The mailbox address. |
| SMTP host | The server name from the mail service or host. |
| Port | 587 for STARTTLS, 465 for SSL. |
| Encryption | **STARTTLS** with port 587, **SSL/TLS** with port 465. |
| Username | Usually the full mailbox address. |
| Password | The mailbox password, or an app password (see below). |
| Allow a local server | Leave off. Turn it on only for a relay on your own network with a self-signed certificate. |

**Test connection** connects, logs in and disconnects. It sends no email. Use **Send test email** to prove a real send.

An SMTP provider reports "Sent" and never reports delivery. SMTP has no webhook.

## Google Workspace and Gmail

1. Turn on 2-Step Verification for the Google account.
2. Create an app password for it in the Google account's security settings. It has 16 characters. Some work, school
   and Advanced Protection accounts can't create one.
3. In AccessBay, use host `smtp.gmail.com`, port 465 with **SSL/TLS** (or port 587 with **STARTTLS**), the full email
   address as the **Username**, and the app password as the **Password**.

Google limits sending to about 2,000 messages a day. Google revokes the app password when the account's password
changes. Then create a new one and enter it in AccessBay.

## Microsoft 365

1. Turn on Authenticated SMTP for the mailbox. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Users > Active users, select
   the user, then Mail > Manage email apps, and tick **Authenticated SMTP**. It stays off when security defaults are
   on.
2. In AccessBay, use host `smtp.office365.com`, port 587 and **STARTTLS**, with the mailbox address and password.

Microsoft is retiring basic authentication for SMTP. Check Microsoft's notice below for the dates. If your tenant no
longer allows it, use an API provider such as [Twilio SendGrid](/guide/providers/sendgrid/) or
[Resend](/guide/providers/resend/) instead.

## Your host's mailbox (cPanel and similar)

1. In your host's control panel, create a mailbox, or use an existing one.
2. Find the mailbox's "mail client settings" page. It lists the outgoing server name, the port and the encryption.
3. Enter those values in AccessBay, with the full mailbox address as the **Username**.

Some hosts limit the number of emails a mailbox can send per hour. Ask your host.

## Common errors

- **The login fails.** Check the user name, the password and that the port matches the encryption.
- **The connection times out.** Your server may block outgoing SMTP ports. Ask your host, or use an API provider.
- **A certificate error.** The host name must match the server's certificate. Use the name the provider gives you.
- **The server refuses the From address.** Most servers only allow the mailbox's own address.

## Vendor documentation

- [Google: send email from an app](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gmail/send-email-from-a-printer-scanner-or-app)
- [Google: app passwords](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833)
- [Microsoft: authenticated client SMTP submission](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/clients-and-mobile-in-exchange-online/authenticated-client-smtp-submission)
- [Microsoft: deprecation of basic authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/clients-and-mobile-in-exchange-online/deprecation-of-basic-authentication-exchange-online)

## SMTP2GO
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/providers/smtp2go/
Description: How to connect SMTP2GO to AccessBay - verify a sender, create an API key, fill in the form and set up delivery events.

AccessBay shows this provider as **SMTP2GO (API)**. It sends through SMTP2GO's web API. To use SMTP2GO's SMTP server
instead, use the [SMTP](/guide/providers/smtp/) provider.

## Before you start

In SMTP2GO, verify a sender address or a whole sending domain. The **From address** in AccessBay must be a verified
sender. SMTP2GO shows the DNS records for a domain in its dashboard. See SMTP2GO's documentation for the free plan's
limits.

## Get the key

1. In SMTP2GO, go to Sending > **API Keys** and add a key.
2. Give the key permission for the email send endpoint (`/email/send`). Leave the other permissions off. The exact
   label in the dashboard may differ.
3. Copy the key. SMTP2GO keys start with `api-`.

## Fill in AccessBay

Go to Settings > Email providers, select **Add provider** and pick **SMTP2GO (API)**.

| AccessBay field | Where the value comes from |
|---|---|
| Name | Any name you like. |
| From address | A verified sender or an address on the verified domain. |
| API key | The key from "Get the key". |
| Region | **Automatic** unless your account is bound to a data region. Then pick United States, Europe or Australia to match it. |
| Webhook username | A user name you choose. Leave empty if you skip webhooks. |
| Webhook password | A password you choose. |
| Webhook bearer token | Optional. A long random value (32 characters or more) that SMTP2GO sends as an `Authorization: Bearer` header, instead of the user name and password. |

SMTP2GO has no way to check a key without sending. **Test connection** sends one test email to your own admin address.
That proves the key, the region and the verified sender.

## Delivery events (webhook)

SMTP2GO doesn't sign webhooks. It can send a basic or bearer authorization header, or a user name and password in the
URL. AccessBay accepts either the user name and password pair or the bearer token, so you can use whichever SMTP2GO
sends. The webhook URL is public, so make the password or token long and random.

1. In AccessBay, copy the **Webhook URL** from the **Webhooks** card.
2. Choose a user name and a password. Enter them in **Webhook username** and **Webhook password** and save.
3. In SMTP2GO, go to Settings > Webhooks > **Manage Webhooks** > **Add Webhook**.
4. Enter the URL with the pair in front of the host: `https://user:password@your-site.example/...`.
5. Choose the users (API keys) it applies to, set the output to **JSON**, and tick the email events.
6. Fill in the **Email headers** option so the message id comes back with each event. Without it, AccessBay can't
   match an event to its email.
7. Save, then use **Test this webhook**.

AccessBay reports these events: delivered, hard bounce, soft bounce, spam, unsubscribe and reject.

## Common errors

- **The test fails.** Check the API key, the region and that the From address is a verified sender.
- **The key is refused.** The key may lack permission for the send endpoint.
- **A wrong region gives authentication errors.** Switch **Region** to **Automatic**, or to the one your account uses.
- **Events arrive but don't match an email.** The custom headers are not ticked in the webhook.

## Vendor documentation

- [Getting started with the API](https://developers.smtp2go.com/docs/getting-started)
- [Set up a webhook](https://developers.smtp2go.com/docs/setup-a-webhook)

## WordPress (wp_mail)
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/providers/wp-mail/
Description: How the WordPress mail provider works in AccessBay, and how to use it with WP Mail SMTP, FluentSMTP or a similar plugin.

**WordPress mail (wp_mail)** hands the email to WordPress's own mail function, `wp_mail()`. It is on the list of
providers from the start, so email works before you set anything up.

## When to choose it

Choose it when a mail plugin, such as WP Mail SMTP, FluentSMTP or Post SMTP, should send AccessBay's emails. Any plugin
that routes `wp_mail()` carries them. AccessBay never replaces `wp_mail()` for the rest of your site.

If no such plugin is installed, WordPress sends with PHP's mail function. Many hosts deliver that poorly or not at all.

## Before you start

Set up the mail plugin first, with the service or SMTP login you want. Follow that plugin's own guide, and send a test
from the plugin. The plugin's service needs a verified sender or domain, like any provider in this guide.

## Fill in AccessBay

There is nothing to fill in. The provider has no key, host or password. It uses the From address of the email, which
the plugin may override.

**Test connection** sends one test email to your own admin address. Use **Send test email** to send to another
address.

## Delivery events (webhook)

Not available. AccessBay can only report that WordPress accepted the email. It can't say whether it arrived. For
delivery events, add an API provider ([Twilio SendGrid](/guide/providers/sendgrid/), [Mailgun](/guide/providers/mailgun/),
[Postmark](/guide/providers/postmark/), [Resend](/guide/providers/resend/), [Brevo](/guide/providers/brevo/) or
[SMTP2GO](/guide/providers/smtp2go/)).

## Common errors

- **AccessBay says "Sent" but the email never arrives.** The plugin can report success while its service rejects the
  message. Check the plugin's own email log, and AccessBay's Email log.
- **Emails go to spam.** The sender or domain isn't authenticated at the plugin's service.
- **"Add a second email provider" notice.** With only `wp_mail`, nothing takes over if it fails. Add another provider.

## Vendor documentation

Your mail plugin's own documentation. WordPress's reference for the function is [wp_mail()](https://developer.wordpress.org/reference/functions/wp_mail/).

## ZeptoMail
