URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/providers/zeptomail/
Description: How to connect ZeptoMail (Zoho) to AccessBay - verify a domain, copy the Send Mail token and fill in the form. Delivery events are not available.

ZeptoMail is Zoho's transactional email service. Zoho's current documentation calls it Zoho CPaaS, and AccessBay
shows it as **ZeptoMail (Zoho CPaaS)**.

## Before you start

In ZeptoMail, add and verify your sending domain on the mail agent you will use. The **From address** must be on that
domain. See ZeptoMail's pricing page for the free tier.

## Get the key

1. In ZeptoMail, go to Mail Agents and open your agent.
2. Open the **SMTP/API** tab, then **API**.
3. Copy the **Send Mail token**, or generate one.

The token may start with `Zoho-enczapikey`. You can include that prefix or leave it out.

## Fill in AccessBay

Go to Settings > Email providers, select **Add provider** and pick **ZeptoMail (Zoho CPaaS)**.

| AccessBay field | Where the value comes from |
|---|---|
| Name | Any name you like. |
| From address | An address on the verified domain. |
| Send Mail token | The token from "Get the key". |
| API host | Leave empty to use `cpaas.zoho.com`. Enter `cpaas.zoho.eu` for the EU data centre. AccessBay also accepts `api.zeptomail.com` and `api.zeptomail.eu`. Use the host that matches your Zoho account's region. |

ZeptoMail has no way to check a token without sending. **Test connection** sends one test email to your own admin
address.

## Delivery events (webhook)

Not available. AccessBay 1.0 has no ZeptoMail delivery events and shows no webhook URL for this provider. An email
sent through ZeptoMail stays at "Sent". For delivered and bounced emails in AccessBay, use another provider.

## Common errors

- **The test fails with an authentication error.** The token is for a different mail agent, or the API host is for
  another region.
- **ZeptoMail refuses the email.** The From address isn't on the verified domain.
- **The API host is refused.** AccessBay accepts only the four hosts listed in the table.

## Vendor documentation

- [ZeptoMail help](https://www.zoho.com/zeptomail/help/)

## Requirements
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/requirements/
Description: The WordPress, PHP and database versions AccessBay needs, and the PHP extensions it checks for.

## Software

| What | Minimum |
|---|---|
| WordPress | 6.8 |
| PHP | 8.3 |
| Database | MySQL 8.0, or MariaDB 10.5, through PHP's `mysqli` extension |

## PHP extensions

AccessBay checks these when you activate it. If one is missing, activation stops with a message that names it, before
anything is written to your database.

- **curl**, with SSL support
- **openssl**
- **mysqli**
- **sodium**, or the copy of sodium_compat that WordPress itself bundles. Without the extension AccessBay still works
  and Site Health notes it.
- A working `random_bytes()`, which every supported PHP version has unless the host has broken it.

After activation, AccessBay keeps checking. If curl or openssl disappears later (after a PHP upgrade, for example),
live mode and outgoing connections switch off until it is back, and Site Health says why.

## Database

- AccessBay's tables use the **InnoDB** engine. A table converted to another engine is reported as critical.
- AccessBay needs every query to reach the **same writable database server**. A set-up that sends some reads to a
  replica (a "split" database drop-in, for example) breaks the locking AccessBay relies on; the health checks detect it
  and switch off the features that depend on it.
- `MYSQL_CLIENT_FLAGS` must not include `MYSQLI_CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS`. With it, the database reports matched rows instead of
  changed rows, and AccessBay's rate limiter could never count correctly, so activation refuses it.

## Scheduled tasks

AccessBay runs its background jobs and health checks on WP-Cron and on normal site traffic. If your site sets
`DISABLE_WP_CRON`, run `wp-cron.php` (or `wp accessbay health`) from a system cron every few minutes. See
[Health checks](/guide/health-checks/).

## The secret key
URL: https://docs.wpanchorbay.com/accessbay/guide/secret-key/
Description: Set ACCESSBAY_SECRET before going live, what happens without it, and how to change it safely.

AccessBay protects the licence keys, tokens and service credentials it stores with keys derived from one site secret,
`ACCESSBAY_SECRET`. The secret lives in your server configuration, never in the database, so a database backup or leak
alone can't open what it protects. It does not depend on WordPress's salts: changing those leaves AccessBay alone.

## Set the secret

1. Generate 32 random bytes:

   ```sh
   openssl rand -base64 32
   ```

2. Add the result to `wp-config.php`, above the line that says "That's all, stop editing!":

   ```php
   define( 'ACCESSBAY_SECRET', 'paste-the-value-here' );
   ```

   Or set an environment variable named `ACCESSBAY_SECRET` for PHP. When both exist, the constant wins.

3. If the site has already run AccessBay without a secret, move its records to the new key:

   ```sh
   wp accessbay keys rotate
   ```

The value must decode to exactly 32 bytes: base64, base64url or 64 hexadecimal characters. Anything else is refused
and Site Health reports it as critical.

<!-- screenshot: Site Health showing the "AccessBay secret and key ids" test as passed -->

Keep a copy of the secret somewhere safe and separate from your database backups. Without it, the records it protects
can't be read.

## Without the secret

- **In test mode**, AccessBay generates a key and stores it in the database, so you can try things out. Site Health
  warns that a generated test-mode key is in use.
- **In live mode**, AccessBay refuses to issue live licences or save live credentials until the secret is defined.
  Site Health reports it as critical, and requests that need it answer `503` with the error code
  `accessbay_temporarily_unavailable`, which means "try again later", never "your key is invalid".

## Change the secret

1. Move the current value into `ACCESSBAY_SECRET_PREVIOUS`, so existing records stay readable. Several old values can
   be listed, separated by commas.
2. Set a new `ACCESSBAY_SECRET`.
3. Run `wp accessbay keys rotate`. It moves every record to the new key and ends with "Every record is under key id
   …". If it warns that records are still under an older key id, run it again. Once it succeeds, you can remove the
   old value from `ACCESSBAY_SECRET_PREVIOUS`.

If records were protected by a secret that is no longer configured, Site Health reports it as critical and those
records answer `503` until you add that secret to `ACCESSBAY_SECRET_PREVIOUS`.

## The public signing key

AccessBay also signs some of its answers so that client software can check they really came from your site.
`wp accessbay keys show` prints the public half of that signing key. It doesn't change when you change the secret.

- GitHub, Composer and Packagist, named in the developer guides.

## Questions

If you own a mark shown here and want it credited differently or removed, write to [support@wpanchorbay.com](mailto:support@wpanchorbay.com).
